US credit stress is intensifying among the weakest-quality borrowers:

Spreads on CCC-rated and lower US corporate bonds are up to 13.3%, near the highest since the 2020 pandemic.

Since January 2026, this figure has surged +490 basis points.

As a result, these spreads have now surpassed the 2022 bear market peak of 12.9%.

For perspective, during the 2020 February-March surge, this metric peaked at 18.8%.

Meanwhile, the spread differential between CCC- and BBB-rated corporate debt has widened to ~1,200 basis points, its widest level in at least 5 years.

This means investors are demanding ~12 percentage points more in compensation to hold the lowest-rated debt rather than first-notch investment-grade corporate bonds.

Cracks are spreading quickly through the lowest-quality credit.

US layoffs continue to slow sharply:

US job cut announcements dropped -71% YoY in October, to 43,994, the lowest October total since 2023.

Year-to-date announcements have declined -44% YoY, to 617,189, the lowest January-October total since 2022.

This is also the 8th month of 2026 with job cuts down YoY versus the corresponding month of the prior year.

Food companies led October layoffs with 9,677 cuts, while Technology has recorded the most reductions year-to-date, at 171,501, up +21% YoY.

Market and economic conditions accounted for 16,407 announced job cuts in October, or ~37% of all layoffs, bringing the year-to-date total to 130,531, overtaking AI as the most cited reason.

US employers appear to be slowing job cuts.

Wiz co-founder and CTO Ami Luttwak says cyberattacks on startups can happen faster than ever:

"I work with the CEOs of startups that are getting attacked. Let's just be in their shoes. You wake up, and your security team says, 'Something bad happened overnight. We tried to stop it, but they got in.'"

"The entire attack, again, takes 20 minutes... from the time they get in until they take all of the secrets, all of the AI keys of all of the customers. And now you have to figure out what are you going to say to all of the customers, and what you're going to do."

"But if I'm a startup, especially if I have anything attackers want... I am on their target. It doesn't have to be a big company."

"If you have AI keys, probably better to put a limit on them, because if they steal them, you don't wanna get a lot of charges, which we see happen a lot, and it's really, really sad. But also make sure that if you have a target on your back, you do need to put a lot of focus on security."

@amiluttwak

Developing a drug takes years, and most candidates never reach patients.

Amortizing the cost of failed drugs across stages, the present value cost of developing a drug is close to $2B. The process takes 13 years on average, with rising clinical trial costs putting further pressure on R&D productivity.

AI could improve those economics by increasing the probability of success and reducing development time, from identifying promising molecules to designing clinical trials and improving patient recruitment.

That may enable companies to pursue therapeutic targets and indications that might otherwise have been uneconomical.

Full piece on why AI will make pharma even bigger: https://t.co/A96FDSSk57

Institutional investors are extremely bullish on the US equity market:

Long non-dealer positioning in US equity futures is up to +$330 billion, its 2nd-highest on record.

This metric covers asset managers, hedge funds, Commodity Trading Advisors (CTAs), and other institutional investors.

Over the last 6 months, net long positioning in US equity futures has risen by +$100 billion.

This figure is now just $10 billion below its all-time high set in 2024.

By comparison, between 2010 and 2023, institutional positioning never exceeded $150 billion.

Institutional investors are heavily exposed to US equities.

Wiz co-founder and CTO Ami Luttwak says AI can now carry out cyberattacks in 20 minutes that once took skilled attackers weeks or months.

In his view, companies need to continuously attack their own systems with the latest AI models to stay secure. For startups, that means building automated testing and patching into the development process from the beginning.

Ami joins a16z's Sarah Wang and Zane Lackey to discuss what changed during Black October, why patching is falling behind, the cost of continuous security testing, and why better security architecture matters more than simply buying more tools.

BREAKING: The US Treasury posted a -$404 billion budget deficit in October, the largest October deficit in history.

This marks a +$120 billion YoY increase and a +$337 billion surge from October 2024.

This comes as government outlays jumped +$84 billion YoY, to $773 billion, their largest for any October on record.

Defense spending was a major driver, surging +$29 billion YoY, to $129 billion, the largest monthly reading in history.

At the same time, government receipts dropped -$35 billion YoY, to $369 billion.

The US deficit crisis is accelerating.

Bitcoin ETF buyers are sitting on losses again, and they're selling.

Bitcoin has dropped below $70,000 for the first time since August, and US spot ETFs have paid $77,108 per coin on average.

BlackRock's fund has seen more than $2.2bn of outflows in ten straight sessions.

The last turn came on 19 August, when the Treasury doubled its long-bond buybacks and Bitcoin ran from $64,700 to $86,600.

@Jamie1Coutts flags a possible retest of the first-half lows near $58,600.

Until liquidity turns again, the daily ETF flow number is the one to watch.

The Nasdaq just fell into a correction. History says the first dip is rarely the low risk buy everyone hopes for.

A 10% pullback from a one year high has happened 77 times in over 50 years, and the first few weeks are barely better than a coin flip. When the drop came fast, with a single day loss over 5%, the index kept falling over the next two weeks in 11 of 18 cases, and more than half of those corrections turned into bear markets.

This week's TradingEdge Weekly video covers why this correction isn't a clean buy yet, a liquidity warning, energy setting up a seasonal window, and longer term signals that have turned favorable.
